title: How do young sunflowers follow the sun?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Do sunflowers turn to face the sun?
Why do grown sunflowers face east?

explain.say: Young sunflower plants track the sun across the sky. In the morning their buds face east, by evening they face west, and during the night they swing back east, ready for sunrise.

explain.say: The trick is uneven growth. During the day the east side of the stem grows faster than the west side, so the top bends steadily westward, following the sun.

explain.say: At night the west side grows faster, turning the head back to face east. An inner body clock times this, so the plant turns in the dark, before the sun has even risen.

explain.say: Once the flowers open, the stem stops growing and the turning stops. Grown sunflowers face east all day, which warms them in the morning, and warm flowers get more visits from bees.

faq.a: Young sunflower plants do, turning from east to west each day and back again at night. Fully grown, blooming sunflowers stop moving and face east.
asks: Do sunflowers turn to face the sun?

faq.q: How does a sunflower turn back at night?
faq.a: At night, cells on the west side of the stem grow faster than those on the east side, swinging the head back to face east by dawn.
asks: Why do sunflowers face east in the morning?

faq.q: How does a sunflower know when to turn?
faq.a: It has an internal circadian clock, a roughly 24-hour timer kept in step with the real sun. In experiments, plants under steady light kept turning for a few days on their own.
asks: Do plants have a body clock?

faq.q: Why do grown sunflowers face east?
faq.a: Facing the morning sun warms the flower head early. A 2016 study found east-facing heads got about five times more visits from bees and other pollinators than west-facing ones.

faq.q: Is following the sun useful to the plant?
faq.a: Yes. Scientists found that young sunflowers allowed to track the sun grew more leaf area and mass than plants that were held still.
asks: Why do sunflowers track the sun?

facts: Only young sunflower plants track the sun; mature flowering heads face east.
A 2016 study in Science found east-facing sunflower heads received about five times as many pollinator visits as west-facing heads.
Turning to follow the sun is called heliotropism.

quiz.say: Which way do fully grown, flowering sunflowers face?
quiz.show: Which way do fully grown, flowering sunflowers face?
quiz.why: Mature heads stop moving and face east, warming up in the morning sun.

wrong.1: They end each day facing west only while young and still growing.
